name: A reading that outvotes the rest
brief:
A pressure sensor logs one whole-number reading per second in `readings`. A reading is the majority when it appears in more than half of the entries. Return it, or `None` when no reading has a majority.

Write `majority_reading(readings)`.

Example. In `[7, 3, 7, 7, 2]` the value 7 appears 3 times out of 5. Three is more than half of five, so the answer is 7.
constraints: $O(n)$ time is the target. Counting each value with `readings.count` is too slow.
All tests share a 5-second time limit.
hint: Count every value in one pass with a dict. Then look for a count above `len(readings) / 2`. Exactly half is not a majority.

examples.note: Seven appears 3 times in 5 readings, which is more than half.
Each value fills exactly half, and half is not more than half.

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: Tally each value once in a dict, then compare each tally with half the length.
The test is strictly more than half, so two values with half each give `None`.
One pass to count and one over the distinct values, so $O(n)$ time and $O(n)$ space.
